stg.policy_snapshots.name: broker_code
stg.policy_snapshots.description: Introducing broker; NULL for direct business. Case and padding vary.

stg.policy_snapshots.name: status
stg.policy_snapshots.description: ACTIVE, EXPIRED, CANCELLED or LAPSED as at the snapshot date (case varies).

stg.policy_snapshots.name: cancellation_date
stg.policy_snapshots.description: Date cover was cancelled, if it was.

stg.policy_snapshots.name: annual_premium
stg.policy_snapshots.description: Annual premium in the policy currency.

stg.policy_snapshots.name: sum_insured
stg.policy_snapshots.description: Sum insured, where the product has one.

stg.policy_snapshots.name: vehicle_reg
stg.policy_snapshots.description: Vehicle registration (motor only). Free text; may be empty or NULL.

stg.policy_snapshots.name: _row_seq
stg.policy_snapshots.description: Position of the row in the extract file.

stg.brokers.name: broker_code
stg.brokers.description: Broker code. Fixed-width, so shorter codes are space-padded.

stg.brokers.name: commission_rate
stg.brokers.description: Commission as a fraction of premium.

stg.brokers.name: appointed_date
stg.brokers.description: Date the broker agency was appointed.

stg.brokers.name: _row_seq
stg.brokers.description: Position of the row in the extract file.

stg.products.name: term_months
stg.products.description: Standard term in months; NULL when the term varies (single-trip travel).

stg.products.name: _row_seq
stg.products.description: Position of the row in the extract file.

contracts.grain: One row per version of a policy (type-2 history): a policy's attributes as they stood from valid_from until valid_to, with a new version opened whenever status, broker, annual premium or vehicle registration changes between snapshots.

columns.name: policy_sk
columns.description: IDENTITY surrogate key that depends on insert order. It is not a business key and will not line up between runs.

columns.name: customer_segment
columns.description: segment_code from dw.dim_customer via a left join. NULL when the customer is not found.

columns.name: broker_code
columns.description: If the source broker is NULL, this is 'DIRECT-SALES', so broker_name is NULL for direct business.

columns.name: broker_name
columns.description: From stg.brokers via a left join. NULL when the broker is not in the register, including DIRECT-SALES.

columns.name: valid_from
columns.description: The snapshot date that opened this version.

columns.name: valid_to
columns.description: 9999-12-31 while the version is current. Once closed, it is the day before the next snapshot that changed it.

columns.name: is_current
columns.description: 'Y' for the open version, 'N' for a closed one.

columns.name: source_snapshot_date
columns.description: The snapshot that inserted the row. Always the same as valid_from.

columns.name: load_ts
columns.description: SYSDATETIME() at insert time, so it depends on when the job ran. It will differ between legacy and the migration.

policy.reason: volatile audit column (estate/jobs.yaml): it changes on every run

cases.description: Letter-case variants across two runs (2025-06-30, then 2025-12-31). Policy 1001 has product_code 'motor01' and the product register has 'MOTOR01'. The legacy inner join still matches it; a binary Spark join drops the policy. Policy 1002 has broker 'brk001' and the register has 'BRK001'. Legacy finds the broker_name; Spark leaves it NULL. In run 2 the changes are case-only: 1001 status 'Active' to 'ACTIVE', 1002 broker 'brk001' to 'BRK001', 1003 vehicle_reg 'ab12cde' to 'AB12CDE'. Legacy opens no new version for these; Spark would close and reopen each one. Policy 1004 is the control: its status really changes, to 'Lapsed'.

Trailing spaces and CHAR padding across two runs. Policy 2001 has product_code 'MOTOR01 ' with a trailing space. The legacy inner join keeps it; Spark drops the policy. Its broker 'BRK1' matches the CHAR(6) register code 'BRK1  ', which is stored padded. Legacy finds the broker_name; Spark gets NULL. Customers 501 and 503 have CHAR(4) segment codes 'GO' and 'STD', which legacy pads to 'GO  ' and 'STD '; Spark leaves them unpadded. Customer 502's 'PLAT' is the canonical 4-character code. In run 2 the only changes are trailing spaces: 2001 status 'Active  ', 2002 broker 'BRK002 ', 2003 vehicle_reg 'CD34EFG  '. Legacy opens no new version for these; Spark would. Policy 2004 is the control: its premium really changes.

ISNULL behaviour across two runs. Policies 3001 and 3004 (run 1) and 3005 (new in run 2) have a NULL broker_code. ISNULL takes the VARCHAR(10) type of p.broker_code, so legacy stores 'DIRECT-SAL'; a Spark coalesce writes 'DIRECT-SALES'. 3001 stays NULL in run 2. Legacy compares 'DIRECT-SAL' with 'DIRECT-SAL' and opens no version. A Spark job that compares the full literal against the stored value, or that mixes the two, can flag a change. 3002 moves vehicle_reg from NULL to '', and 3003 from '' to NULL. Under ISNULL(...,'') these are equal and no version opens; a null-safe Spark compare would open one. 3004 is the control: its broker really changes, from NULL to BRK001. NULL status or premium cannot be tested here because both columns are NOT NULL in staging.
